title: Now the co-culture experiment: when ΔrhlI and ΔlasI are grown together, do they…

turns.text: Now the co-culture experiment: when ΔrhlI and ΔlasI are grown together, do they swarm like wild type again, and does it depend on the ratio they are mixed at? I care about where the peak is and how strong the ratio effect is. Same rules: R, a figure and a table in results/. One clean figure is enough — do not spend several rounds restyling it.

output.text:
- Used circularity as the primary shape readout and roundness as a check on elongation (the usual reading of these imaging-software metrics; the data sheet does not give their formulas). The two disagree in a useful way: circularity changes strongly while roundness does not, which points to the colony perimeter rather than elongation. See [results/swarming_single_mutants_summary.csv](results/swarming_single_mutants_summary.csv).
- Added a secondary comparison of rhl mutants against las mutants, pooling the two mutants of each system (6 vs 6 dishes). It is exploratory, not a pre-specified contrast; the per-mutant results show the same ordering. See [results/swarming_system_contrast.csv](results/swarming_system_contrast.csv).

### Files

- [analysis/swarming_single_mutants.R](analysis/swarming_single_mutants.R) — the analysis: data reading, Welch comparisons, assumption checks, sensitivity analyses and the figure; writes the three result files.
- [results/swarming_single_mutants_summary.csv](results/swarming_single_mutants_summary.csv) — one row per genotype: area, circularity and roundness means and SDs, ratios or differences versus wild type with 95% CIs, and Holm-adjusted p-values.
- [results/swarming_system_contrast.csv](results/swarming_system_contrast.csv) — rhl mutants versus las mutants for area, circularity and roundness.
- [results/swarming_single_mutants.png](results/swarming_single_mutants.png) — three-panel figure of area, circularity and roundness by genotype.

### To do

- [x] Explore the swarming data and check distributions
- [x] Write and run the R analysis
- [x] Write figure and numeric table to results/

## Data

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| [data/swarming/single_cultures.csv](data/swarming/single_cultures.csv) | Swarming of wild type and the four single mutants, one dish per row: the colony `area` and `circularity` the imaging software reports, three replicates each. |
| [data/swarming/cocultures.csv](data/swarming/cocultures.csv) | Swarming of wild type, ΔlasI and ΔrhlI grown alone, and of ΔrhlI:ΔlasI mixes at eleven ratios from 1:3 to 1000:1, three replicates each. `ratio_rhlI_to_lasI` reads ΔrhlI first, so 10:1 is ten ΔrhlI cells per ΔlasI cell. |
| [data/rnaseq/counts.csv](data/rnaseq/counts.csv) | Raw RNA-seq counts, one row per gene and one column per sample. |
| [data/rnaseq/samples.csv](data/rnaseq/samples.csv) | What each sample column is: `Media` (MMGluFeMinus, MMGluFePlus, Succinate) × `Strain` (1 wild type, 97 ΔrhlI, 98 ΔlasI, 99 ΔlasIΔrhlI) × `Replicate` (A, B, C). |
| [data/rnaseq/annotation.csv](data/rnaseq/annotation.csv) | Each locus tag's gene name and product. |

The data come with the study
([microPublication Biology, 10.17912/micropub.biology.001326](https://doi.org/10.17912/micropub.biology.001326));
the counts and sample sheet are as distributed with it, and the annotation keeps the three
columns this project reads.

## Notes

`area` is in the units the imaging software reports, so it is compared within the assay and
never across assays. The swarming assay has three replicates per condition.

steps.text:
Yes — co-culture restores swarming, and the ratio matters strongly.

**Peak.** The fitted optimum is **12.3:1 ΔrhlI:ΔlasI** (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI **10.4–14.7:1**). At the peak, fitted area is **145,880** versus a wild-type geometric mean of **108,686** — **1.34× wild type** (95% CI **0.99–1.71**). The nearest observed mix, 10:1, was 1.64× wild type (0.83–3.25, unadjusted p = 0.11), so the peak is statistically indistinguishable from wild type, not significantly above it. For comparison, ΔrhlI alone was 0.094× and ΔlasI alone 0.134× wild type, so the peak is about 14× and 10× their own areas.

**Ratio effect.** Across the ten well-sampled ratios (1:3–100:1), the mixing ratio explains **93% of the variance in log area** (one-way ANOVA F(9,20) = 29.5, p = 1.2 × 10⁻⁹; quadratic R² = 0.891 versus 0.364 for a linear fit). The fitted peak is **8.7×** the 1:3 value, **2.1×** the 100:1 value and **14.5×** the 500:1 value. Fitted area reaches wild-type level between **3.2:1 and 46.4:1**. Beyond that, rescue collapses at 500:1 (0.09× wild type, the only mix significantly below wild type after Holm, p = 0.037) and is heterogeneous at 1000:1 (0.34×, CI 0.06–2.14). Shape converges on the same optimum: circularity reaches its minimum at 12.2:1 and roundness its maximum at 12.2:1.

**Caveats.** Three dishes per condition; the low-ratio pairwise reductions (0.17–0.39× wild type) are only borderline after Holm correction (p = 0.073–0.121), so the overall model carries that part of the conclusion. The peak location depends on the fitted window: including all twelve ratios gives 15.6:1 but a poor fit (R² 0.66), while excluding only 500:1 or only 1000:1 gives 22.4:1 or 11.2:1. Within the observed rescue window, leave-one-ratio-out peaks span 11.6–13.1.

Files:
- [analysis/swarming_cocultures.R](analysis/swarming_cocultures.R) — full analysis, reproduces everything with `Rscript analysis/swarming_cocultures.R`
- [results/swarming_cocultures_summary.csv](results/swarming_cocultures_summary.csv) — per-condition table with comparisons versus wild type
- [results/swarming_cocultures_ratio_model.csv](results/swarming_cocultures_ratio_model.csv) — peak, ratio effect, sensitivity and diagnostic table
- [results/swarming_cocultures.png](results/swarming_cocultures.png) — one three-panel figure (area, circularity, roundness)
